source.text: Ὅτε οὖν ἔνιψεν τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν καὶ ἔλαβεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνέπεσεν, πάλιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γινώσκετε τί πεποίηκα ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: When therefore he washed the feet of them and took the garments of him and reclined, again he said to them, "Do you know what I have done to you?

en.L: So when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had washed their feet and taken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments and reclined, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them again, "Do you know what I have done to you?
en.B: When Jesus had washed their feet, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outer clothes back on and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them again: "Do you understand what I have done for you?
en.R: After Jesus had washed their feet, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outer clothes back on and went back to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them again. "Do you understand what I have done for you?

es.L: Así que, cuando les lavó los pies y tomó su manto y se recostó [a la mesa], les dijo otra vez: «¿{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he hecho?
es.B: Cuando Jesús terminó de lavarles los pies, se volvió a poner el manto y ocupó de nuevo su lugar a la mesa. Entonces les habló otra vez: «¿{{plural_you:Entienden lo que he hecho por ustedes|Entendéis lo que he hecho por vosotros}}?
es.R: Después de lavarles los pies, Jesús se volvió a poner la ropa y regresó a su lugar a la mesa. Entonces les habló otra vez. «¿{{plural_you:Entienden lo que he hecho por ustedes|Entendéis lo que he hecho por vosotros}}?

sw.L: Basi alipokwisha kuwaosha miguu, na kuyachukua mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuketi mezani, akawaambia tena, "Mnajua niliyowatendea?
sw.B: Yesu alipomaliza kuwaosha miguu, alivaa tena mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya nje, akarudi mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani. Kisha akasema nao tena: "Mnaelewa niliyowatendea?
sw.R: Baada ya Yesu kuwaosha miguu, alivaa tena nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} za nje, akarudi mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani. Kisha akasema nao tena. "Mnaelewa niliyowatendea?

vi.L: Vậy khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã rửa chân họ, mặc áo vào và ngả mình [bên bàn ăn] lại, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nói với họ: "Các con có biết điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho các con không?
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu đã rửa chân cho các môn đồ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mặc áo ngoài vào và trở lại chỗ ngồi bên bàn ăn. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nói với họ: "Các con có hiểu việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vừa làm cho các con không?
vi.R: Rửa chân cho các môn đồ xong, Đức Giê-xu mặc áo ngoài vào và trở về chỗ mình bên bàn ăn. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nói với họ: "Các con có hiểu việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vừa làm cho các con không?

ko.L: 그러므로 그분이 그들의 발을 씻기시고 자기 겉옷을 입으시고 [식탁에] 기대어 앉으신 뒤에, 그들에게 다시 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희에게 한 일을 너희가 아느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서는 그들의 발을 씻기신 뒤에 겉옷을 다시 입으시고 식탁의 자기 자리에 앉으셨다. 그리고 그들에게 다시 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희에게 해 준 일을 너희가 깨닫겠느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 그들의 발을 다 씻기신 뒤에, 겉옷을 다시 입으시고 식탁의 자리로 돌아와 앉으셨다. 그리고 그들에게 다시 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희에게 해 준 일을 알겠느냐?

decisions.choice: again goes with "said": he spoke to them again (SBLGNT punctuation)
alternatives: again goes with "reclined": he reclined again, then said
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts its comma before "again", so the word begins the next clause: having taken his place, Jesus spoke to them again, after the exchange with Peter (13:6-11). Other editions put the comma after it, giving "reclined again". The sense hardly changes: he had got up from the meal (13:4), so taking his place at the table is a return either way.

decisions.choice: a question: Do you know what I have done to you?
alternatives: a command: Understand what I have done to you
decisions.reason: The verb form is the same for "you know" and "know!", so the words could be a question or a command. The SBLGNT prints a question, and Jesus goes on to explain the act himself (13:13-17), as a teacher does after asking his pupils. Either way he takes up what he said to Peter: "what I am doing you do not know now, but you will understand afterward" (13:7). The footnote gives the command.

decisions.choice: took his garments and reclined: he dressed again and returned to his place at the meal
decisions.reason: He had laid aside his outer garments to wash their feet (13:4). At a formal meal guests reclined on couches around a low table, leaning on the left elbow, so "reclined" means he took his place at the table again. The same pair of verbs, laying down and taking up, is used of his life in 10:17-18; John may intend the echo, so that the washing pictures his death and return, but he does not say so.

decisions.choice: Jesus (subject); outer clothes back on; took his place at the table (B), went back to his place at the table (R)
alternatives: he had washed; taken his garments; reclined (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last speaker in the scene was Peter (13:9). "Outer clothes" says what the garments were (meaning decision m3), and "took his place at the table" says what reclining at a meal meant.

decisions.choice: Do you understand ... for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The question is about grasping the meaning of the act, which "understand" says. The washing was done to them and for their good, so Balanced and Readable say "for you"; Literal keeps "to you".

decisions.choice: ¿Entienden lo que he hecho por ustedes?
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific -si- and 께서 at every level (style guide section 7).

source.text: ὑμεῖς φωνεῖτέ με Ὁ διδάσκαλος καὶ Ὁ κύριος, καὶ καλῶς λέγετε, εἰμὶ γάρ.

records.literal_gloss: You call me 'the Teacher' and 'the Lord', and well you say, I am for.

en.L: You call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'the Teacher' and 'the Lord,' and you say [it] well, for I am [so].
en.B: You call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and you are right, because that is what I am.
en.R: You call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} your Teacher and your Lord. And you are right, because that is who I am.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes me llaman|Vosotros me llamáis}} “el Maestro” y “el Señor”, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} bien, porque lo soy.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes me llaman|Vosotros me llamáis}} “Maestro” y “Señor”, y {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} razón, porque lo soy.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes me llaman su|Vosotros me llamáis vuestro}} Maestro y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Señor. Y {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} razón, porque eso es lo que soy.

sw.L: Ninyi mnaniita 'Mwalimu' na 'Bwana,' nanyi mnasema vizuri, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye.
sw.B: Ninyi mnaniita 'Mwalimu' na 'Bwana,' nanyi mko sahihi, kwa sababu ndivyo nilivyo.
sw.R: Ninyi mnaniita Mwalimu wenu na Bwana wenu. Nanyi mko sahihi, kwa sababu hivyo ndivyo nilivyo.

vi.L: Các con gọi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là 'Thầy' và 'Chúa', và các con nói phải, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [đúng là thế].
vi.B: Các con gọi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là 'Thầy' và 'Chúa', và các con nói đúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đúng là như vậy.
vi.R: Các con gọi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Thầy và là Chúa của các con. Các con nói đúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thật là như thế.

ko.L: 너희는 나를 '선생님', 그리고 '주님'이라고 부르는데, 너희가 말을 잘 하였다. 내가 [그러하기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 너희는 나를 '선생님', '주님' 하고 부른다. 너희 말이 옳다. 나는 정말 그러하다.
ko.R: 너희는 나를 너희의 선생님이며 주님이라고 부른다. 너희 말이 맞다. 내가 바로 그렇기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the Teacher and the Lord: titles, as the disciples addressed him
alternatives: the teacher and the lord as plain descriptions
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand in the naming case with the article, the way a title or a form of address is quoted. "Teacher" is John's own translation of "Rabbi" (1:38; 20:16), the name the disciples use for him (1:49; 4:31; 11:8). Jesus is repeating the titles they actually use.

decisions.choice: Lord: the disciples' title of respect for their master and teacher, which in John comes to mean more
decisions.reason: A disciple called his teacher "lord" as a mark of respect and of belonging to him, and the disciples use it throughout (6:68; 11:12; 13:6, 9). Jesus accepts the title. In John its meaning grows until Thomas says "My Lord and my God" (20:28). Here it sets up the argument of 13:14 and the saying about master and slave in 13:16, where the same word means a slave's owner.

decisions.choice: for I am: for I am the Teacher and the Lord; the predicate comes from the sentence
decisions.reason: "I am" here simply agrees with what they say: the titles they have just used are its complement. It is not the bare, unexplained "I am" of 13:19, where nothing in the sentence completes it.

decisions.choice: Teacher and Lord, capitalised; in quotation marks (L, B)
decisions.reason: They are titles for Jesus, so they are capitalised at every level, and "Lord" follows the book-wide choice for his disciples' address. Literal keeps the article ("the Teacher"); Readable says "your Teacher and your Lord" to make the titles plain without quotation marks.

decisions.choice: you say [it] well, for I am [so] (L); you are right, because that is what I am (B, R)
decisions.reason: A bare "for I am" would look like the absolute "I am" of 13:19; every level supplies the complement (meaning decision m3), Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: Maestro y Señor, capitalised; in inner quotation marks (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decisions m1, m2). Spanish "lo soy" needs no supplied word.

decisions.choice: 'Mwalimu' na 'Bwana', capitalised; in quotation marks (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the English: these are the titles the disciples use, so they are capitalised and, at Literal and Balanced, quoted. "Bwana" is the disciples' Lord, as in verse 6; in verse 16 the master of a slave is "bwana" in lower case.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" and "Chúa"
decisions.reason: These are the very words the disciples use to address Jesus in this translation ("Thầy" for Teacher and Rabbi, "Chúa" for kyrie), so the saying matches how they speak to him.

decisions.choice: '선생님', '주님' as the disciples' titles for Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the way the disciples address him, so the titles keep the honorific 님 they would use; when he names himself in verse 14 he says 주, 선생 without it.

source.text: εἰ οὖν ἐγὼ ἔνιψα ὑμῶν τοὺς πόδας ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ διδάσκαλος, καὶ ὑμεῖς ὀφείλετε ἀλλήλων νίπτειν τοὺς πόδας·

records.literal_gloss: If therefore I washed of you the feet, the Lord and the Teacher, also you ought of one another to wash the feet;

en.L: If then I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
en.B: So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, then you too have a duty to wash each other's feet.
en.R: I am your Lord and your Teacher, and I have washed your feet. So you also should wash each other's feet.

es.L: Pues si yo, el Señor y el Maestro, {{plural_you:les|os}} lavé los pies, también {{plural_you:ustedes deben lavarse|vosotros debéis lavaros}} los pies unos a otros.
es.B: Así que, si yo, el Señor y el Maestro, {{plural_you:les|os}} he lavado los pies, también {{plural_you:ustedes tienen el deber de lavarse|vosotros tenéis el deber de lavaros}} los pies unos a otros.
es.R: Yo soy {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Señor y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Maestro, y {{plural_you:les|os}} he lavado los pies. Así que también {{plural_you:ustedes deben lavarse|vosotros debéis lavaros}} los pies unos a otros.

sw.L: Basi ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, Bwana na Mwalimu, niliwaosha miguu, ninyi nanyi mnapaswa kuoshana miguu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, Bwana na Mwalimu, nimewaosha miguu, basi ninyi pia mna wajibu wa kuoshana miguu.
sw.R: Mimi ni Bwana wenu na Mwalimu wenu, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nimewaosha miguu. Kwa hiyo ninyi pia mnapaswa kuoshana miguu.

vi.L: Vậy nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là Chúa và là Thầy, đã rửa chân cho các con, thì các con cũng phải rửa chân cho nhau.
vi.B: Vậy, nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Chúa và là Thầy mà còn rửa chân cho các con, thì các con cũng có bổn phận rửa chân cho nhau.
vi.R: Ta là Chúa và là Thầy của các con, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã rửa chân cho các con. Vậy các con cũng nên rửa chân cho nhau.

ko.L: 그러므로 주이며 선생인 내가 너희의 발을 씻겼으니, 너희도 서로의 발을 씻겨 주어야 한다.
ko.B: 그러니 주이며 선생인 내가 너희의 발을 씻겼다면, 너희도 마땅히 서로의 발을 씻겨 주어야 한다.
ko.R: 나는 너희의 주이고 선생이다. 그런 내가 너희의 발을 씻겨 주었다. 그러니 너희도 서로의 발을 씻겨 주어야 한다.

decisions.choice: an argument from the greater to the lesser: since I, the Lord, did this, you can hardly refuse
decisions.reason: "If" here states a fact: he has washed their feet. Jesus now puts "Lord" before "Teacher", reversing the order of 13:13, which stresses his rank. If the one with the highest place did the lowest task, none of them can think it beneath him. The point returns as a saying in 13:16.

decisions.choice: washing feet: a slave's task, done for guests
decisions.reason: Roads were dusty and people wore sandals, so a host's slave washed the feet of guests (compare 1 Samuel 25:41, where Abigail offers to wash the feet of David's servants). A free man would not normally do it for his equals, still less a teacher for his disciples; this is why Peter objects (13:6-8).

decisions.choice: ought to wash one another's feet: the disciples are to serve one another as he served them, in the humblest tasks; whether the washing itself is also meant as a practice is left open
alternatives: a command to repeat the washing of feet as a regular practice
only a picture of humble service, not meant literally
decisions.reason: "Ought" is the language of a debt: what he has done puts them under an obligation to one another. Verse 15 calls the washing an example, and in 13:34 and 15:12 the command is to love one another as he loved them, which points beyond the act itself. But the early church did wash the feet of fellow believers: 1 Timothy 5:10 lists "washed the feet of the saints" among a widow's good works. The text supports at least humble service of one another; how far it also asks for the literal act is a judgment.

decisions.choice: have a duty to (B), should (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to owe, and so to be bound to do something. Balanced says "have a duty to" to keep the sense of a debt; Readable uses the plain "should". Readable turns the condition into two statements of fact, since the "if" assumes the washing happened (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: deben lavarse / debéis lavaros
decisions.reason: The reflexive changes with the plural, so it sits inside the ustedes / vosotros span.

decisions.choice: 주, 선생 without 님 when Jesus names himself
decisions.reason: Korean speakers do not attach the honorific 님 to themselves; the plain titles say the same thing in Jesus's own mouth.

source.text: ὑπόδειγμα γὰρ ἔδωκα ὑμῖν ἵνα καθὼς ἐγὼ ἐποίησα ὑμῖν καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: An example for I gave you, that just as I did to you also you may do.

en.L: For I gave you an example, so that just as I did to you, you also may do.
en.B: What I gave you was an example, so that you also would do as I have done for you.
en.R: I have given you an example to follow. You should do for each other what I have done for you.

es.L: Porque ejemplo {{plural_you:les|os}} di, para que, como yo {{plural_you:les|os}} hice, también {{plural_you:ustedes hagan|vosotros hagáis}}.
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado es un ejemplo, para que también {{plural_you:ustedes hagan|vosotros hagáis}} lo que yo he hecho por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado un ejemplo para que lo {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}}. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} unos por otros lo que yo he hecho por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana niliwapa mfano, ili ninyi pia mfanye kama vile {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nilivyowafanyia.
sw.B: Nilichowapa ni mfano, ili ninyi pia mfanye kama nilivyowafanyia.
sw.R: Nimewapa mfano wa kufuata. Mnapaswa kufanyiana yale niliyowafanyia.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho các con một tấm gương, để như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho các con, thì các con cũng làm như vậy.
vi.B: Điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã cho các con là một tấm gương, để các con cũng làm như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho các con.
vi.R: Ta đã cho các con một tấm gương để noi theo. Các con hãy làm cho nhau điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho các con.

ko.L: 내가 너희에게 본보기를 주었기 때문이다. 내가 너희에게 한 그대로 너희도 하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 준 것은 본보기이다. 내가 너희에게 한 것처럼 너희도 하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 너희가 따라야 할 본보기를 보여 주었다. 내가 너희에게 해 준 것처럼 너희도 서로에게 해 주어야 한다.

decisions.choice: example: a pattern given to be copied
alternatives: a mere illustration or object lesson
decisions.reason: The word means a pattern or model that others are meant to follow (James 5:10 uses it of the prophets as an example of patient suffering). The purpose clause that follows says the same: "so that you also may do".

decisions.choice: just as I did to you: the same kind of service, given in the same love
decisions.reason: "Just as" asks for more than copying the outward act: it asks them to serve as he served. John opens the scene with Jesus loving his own to the end (13:1), and the command of 13:34 has the same shape: "just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another". So the example reaches to the self-giving that the washing pictures (meaning decision m3 at 13:14).

decisions.choice: for: the example explains the duty of 13:14; "example" stands first for emphasis
decisions.reason: "For" gives the reason they owe one another this service: he did it as an example. The word stands first in the sentence, so the stress falls on it: what he did was meant to be followed.

decisions.choice: What I gave you was an example (B); an example to follow ... for each other (R)
alternatives: For I have given you an example (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the weight on "example" by putting it at the end of its clause (meaning decision m3). Readable adds "to follow" and "for each other", which come from the purpose clause and from 13:14.

decisions.choice: Porque ejemplo les di
decisions.reason: Literal puts "ejemplo" first, as the Greek does for emphasis (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ἀπόστολος μείζων τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, not is a slave greater than the master of him, nor a sent one greater than the [one] having sent him.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor [is] a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, a servant is not greater than his master, and one who is sent is not greater than the one who sent him.
en.R: I tell you the truth: a servant is not more important than his master. And a messenger is not more important than the person who sent him.

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: el esclavo no es mayor que su señor, ni el enviado mayor que el que lo envió.
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el siervo no es más que su señor, ni el enviado es más que el que lo envió.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: un siervo no es más importante que su señor. Y un mensajero no es más importante que el que lo envió.

sw.L: Kweli kweli nawaambia, mtumwa si mkuu kuliko bwana wake, wala mjumbe si mkuu kuliko yule aliyemtuma.
sw.B: Kweli kweli nawaambia, mtumishi hamzidi bwana wake, na aliyetumwa hamzidi yule aliyemtuma.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: mtumishi si muhimu kuliko bwana wake. Na mjumbe si muhimu kuliko mtu aliyemtuma.

vi.L: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, nô lệ không lớn hơn chủ mình, sứ giả cũng không lớn hơn người đã sai mình.
vi.B: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con: Đầy tớ không lớn hơn chủ mình, người được sai đi cũng không lớn hơn người đã sai mình.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: Đầy tớ không quan trọng hơn chủ mình. Sứ giả cũng không quan trọng hơn người đã sai mình.

ko.L: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 종은 자기 주인보다 크지 않고, 보냄을 받은 자가 자기를 보낸 사람보다 크지 않다.
ko.B: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 종은 자기 주인보다 높지 않고, 보냄을 받은 사람은 자기를 보낸 사람보다 높지 않다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 종은 자기 주인보다 더 중요하지 않다. 심부름 간 사람은 자기를 보낸 사람보다 더 중요하지 않다.

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master, with no rights of his own
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary one for a slave, someone who was another's property (8:34-35). In the household picture of this saying the slave owes everything to the master and has no standing above him. Jesus has just done a slave's task (13:14); his disciples are in the slave's place and cannot claim to be above it.

decisions.choice: his master: an ordinary owner in the saying, but the word is the one the disciples use for Jesus
decisions.reason: In the saying the master is simply a slave's owner. The word is the same as "Lord" in 13:13-14, so the hearers apply it at once: if their Lord has washed feet, his slaves cannot refuse to. Jesus repeats the saying in 15:20 to warn them that they will share his treatment; Matthew 10:24 has a similar saying.

decisions.choice: messenger: one sent on another's behalf, an envoy
alternatives: apostle, as the title of the Twelve
decisions.reason: This is the only time the noun occurs in John. It comes from the verb "to send" and here means anyone sent with a task, as the parallel "the one who sent him" shows; it is not yet the title of an office. An envoy acted with his sender's authority but was never above him (compare 12:44-45 and 13:20). The disciples are about to be sent (17:18; 20:21).

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 13:20 as well.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R); master; messenger (L, R), one who is sent (B)
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable and "slave" in Literal, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the slave was owned. "Master" is used because in the saying the word means an owner of slaves, not the title of 13:13 (meaning decision m2). "Apostle" would suggest the later office (meaning decision m3); Balanced says "one who is sent" so that the link with "the one who sent him" stays visible. "His" refers to the figure in the saying, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: esclavo (L), siervo (B, R); señor
decisions.reason: "Señor" rather than "amo" keeps the link with the title the disciples use for Jesus in verses 13-14 (meaning decision m2). "Enviado" (L, B) and "mensajero" (R), as in English.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L), mtumishi (B, R); bwana wake, lowercase; mjumbe (L, R), aliyetumwa (B)
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" (servant) in Balanced and Readable and "mtumwa" (slave) in Literal, as the English has it (meaning decision m1). The master in the saying is an ordinary owner, so "bwana" is lowercase and "wake" carries no reader setting. "Mtume" would read as "apostle", a title the Gospel of John never uses; "mjumbe" is any messenger, the sense in the meaning note.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R)
decisions.reason: The double "amen" as the style guide sets it for the whole book; also in verse 20.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L), "đầy tớ" (B, R); "sứ giả" (L, R), "người được sai đi" (B)
decisions.reason: doulos as the style guide sets it; the messenger is named as one sent, matching "người đã sai mình".

decisions.choice: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다 (L, B); 내가 분명히 말한다 (R)
decisions.reason: The guide's book-wide rendering of amen amen (one decision for the passage, also verse 20).

source.text: εἰ ταῦτα οἴδατε, μακάριοί ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: If these things you know, blessed are you if you do them.

en.L: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
en.B: Now you know these things; you are blessed if you act on them.
en.R: Now you know these things. If you do them, God's blessing is on you.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} estas cosas, dichosos {{plural_you:son|sois}} si las {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}.
es.B: Ya {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} estas cosas; dichosos {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} si las {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} en práctica.
es.R: Ya {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} estas cosas. Si las {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} bendecirá.

sw.L: Kama mnayajua mambo haya, heri yenu mkiyafanya.
sw.B: Sasa mnayajua mambo haya; mmebarikiwa mkiyatekeleza.
sw.R: Sasa mnajua mambo haya. Mkiyafanya, baraka ya Mungu iko juu yenu.

vi.L: Nếu các con biết những điều này, các con có phước nếu các con làm theo.
vi.B: Bây giờ các con đã biết những điều này; các con có phước nếu làm theo.
vi.R: Bây giờ các con đã biết những điều này. Nếu các con làm theo, các con sẽ được Đức Chúa Trời ban phước.

ko.L: 너희가 이것들을 알면, 그것들을 행할 때 너희는 복이 있다.
ko.B: 이제 너희가 이것을 알았으니, 그대로 행하면 복이 있다.
ko.R: 이제 너희는 이것을 안다. 이것을 그대로 행하면, 하나님께서 너희에게 복을 주신다.

decisions.choice: two different conditions: since you know (a fact), if you do (still open)
decisions.reason: The first "if" assumes what it states: they now know, because he has shown and explained it. The second "if" leaves the matter open: whether they will do it remains to be seen. Knowing is not yet blessing; doing is what counts (compare James 1:25).

decisions.choice: blessed: in a good state in God's sight, favored by him
alternatives: happy, in the sense of a feeling
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in the beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-11) and in the Psalms (Psalm 1:1 in Greek). It declares a person well off before God, whatever they feel. It occurs twice in John, here and in 20:29 ("blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed").

decisions.choice: Now you know (B, R); act on them (B); God's blessing is on you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the first condition as the fact it assumes (meaning decision m1). Balanced says "act on them" for doing what one has learned. "Blessed" is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable names God as the one who blesses, which the word implies (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: dichosos (L, B); Dios los bendecirá (R)
decisions.reason: Favored in God's sight (meaning decision m2). "Bienaventurados" is the traditional word but now sounds old; Readable says whose blessing it is, as in English.

decisions.choice: "có phước"
decisions.reason: "có phước" says that God favours them, which is the sense of the Greek; "hạnh phúc" would make it a feeling.

source.text: οὐ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν λέγω· ἐγὼ οἶδα τίνας ἐξελεξάμην· ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ· Ὁ τρώγων μου τὸν ἄρτον ἐπῆρεν ἐπ’ ἐμὲ τὴν πτέρναν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not about all of you I speak; I know whom I chose; but that the scripture may be fulfilled, 'The [one] eating of me the bread lifted up against me the heel of him.'

en.L: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I chose. But [this is] so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: 'The one who eats {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bread has lifted up his heel against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.B: I am not speaking of all of you. I know the ones I chose. But it is happening so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: 'The one who eats {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bread has raised his heel against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But what the Scripture says must come true: 'The one who shares {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bread has turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

es.L: No hablo de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; yo sé a quiénes elegí. Pero [esto es] para que se cumpla la Escritura: “El que come mi pan levantó contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} su talón”.
es.B: No hablo de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Yo sé a quiénes he elegido. Pero esto sucede para que se cumpla la Escritura: “El que come mi pan ha levantado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} su talón”.
es.R: No estoy hablando de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Yo conozco a los que he elegido. Pero tiene que cumplirse lo que dice la Escritura: “El que comparte mi pan se ha vuelto contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}”.

sw.L: Sisemi juu ya ninyi nyote; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawajua wale niliowachagua. Lakini [ni] ili Maandiko yatimie: 'Yule anayekula mkate {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ameinua kisigino chake dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.'
sw.B: Sisemi juu yenu nyote. Nawajua wale niliowachagua. Lakini hili linatokea ili Maandiko yatimie: 'Yule anayekula mkate {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ameinua kisigino chake dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.'
sw.R: Sisemi juu yenu nyote. Nawajua wale niliowachagua. Lakini yale Maandiko yasemayo lazima yatimie: 'Yule anayeshiriki mkate {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} amegeuka kunipinga.'

vi.L: Ta không nói về tất cả các con; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết những ai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn. Nhưng [việc này xảy ra] để Kinh Thánh được ứng nghiệm: 'Người ăn bánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giơ gót chân lên chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'
vi.B: Ta không nói về tất cả các con. Ta biết những người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn. Nhưng việc này xảy ra để lời Kinh Thánh được ứng nghiệm: 'Kẻ ăn bánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giơ gót lên chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'
vi.R: Ta không nói về tất cả các con. Ta biết những người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn. Nhưng lời Kinh Thánh phải được ứng nghiệm: 'Người cùng ăn bánh với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã quay lại chống nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'

ko.L: 내가 너희 모두에 관하여 말하는 것은 아니다. 나는 내가 누구를 택하였는지 안다. 그러나 [이것은] 성경이 이루어지게 하려는 것이다. '내 빵을 먹는 자가 나를 향해 자기 발꿈치를 들었다.'
ko.B: 내가 너희 모두를 두고 하는 말이 아니다. 나는 내가 택한 사람들을 안다. 그러나 이 일은 성경 말씀이 이루어지려고 일어나는 것이다. '내 빵을 먹는 사람이 나를 향해 발꿈치를 들었다.'
ko.R: 내가 너희 모두에 대해 말하는 것이 아니다. 나는 내가 택한 사람들을 알고 있다. 그러나 성경에 있는 이 말씀이 이루어져야 한다. '내 빵을 함께 먹는 사람이 나에게 등을 돌렸다.'

decisions.choice: I know whom I chose: he chose all twelve, Judas among them, and was not deceived about any of them
alternatives: he knows which of them are truly his chosen ones, and Judas is not among them (15:16)
decisions.reason: Jesus has just said that not all of them are clean (13:10-11). In 6:70 he says "Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil", and 6:64 says he knew from the beginning who would betray him. So the point is most likely that the betrayal will not take him by surprise. In 15:16 "I chose you" is said to the disciples who remain after Judas has gone, which allows the other reading.

decisions.choice: but so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: words are left out; the sense is "but this is happening so that"
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "but so that the Scripture may be fulfilled", with no main verb. The missing words are understood from the context: the choosing of a betrayer and what he is about to do happen so that Scripture is fulfilled. John uses the same short form in 9:3 and 15:25. "The Scripture" here means one particular passage.

decisions.choice: Psalm 41:10, quoted freely
decisions.reason: In the psalm the speaker, a righteous sufferer traditionally identified as David, laments that even his close friend, who ate his bread, has turned against him. John's wording is closer to the Hebrew than to the Greek translation of the Psalms and leaves out the words about the friend "in whom I trusted". To eat a man's bread was to share his table and his friendship, so the betrayal comes from the closest circle (13:26). Reviewers should check the wording against the Greek and Hebrew of the psalm.

decisions.choice: lifted up his heel against me: has turned against me with contempt, as a betrayer
alternatives: tripping someone up, as a wrestler does
decisions.reason: The exact picture is uncertain: raising the heel may be the movement of a kick, of showing someone the sole of the foot as an insult, or of tripping an opponent. All of them express hostility and contempt from someone who should have been loyal. The past tense comes from the psalm; for Jesus the act is about to happen.

decisions.choice: eats: the verb John uses in 6:54-58, possibly an echo
alternatives: an ordinary word for eating, with no echo
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for eating the flesh of the Son of Man (6:54-58) and here; elsewhere in the New Testament it occurs only in Matthew 24:38. The echo would sharpen the irony: one who shared the table of the one who gives himself as bread turns against him. But the verb was also an everyday word for eating, so the link is possible, not certain.

decisions.choice: raised his heel against me (B); shares my bread, has turned against me (R)
alternatives: has lifted up his heel against me (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture, as the psalm does. Readable gives the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m4), and says "shares my bread" because eating someone's bread meant sharing their table (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: [this is] so that (L); it is happening so that (B); what the Scripture says must come true (R)
alternatives: but so that the Scripture may be fulfilled (no words supplied)
decisions.reason: English needs a main verb here (meaning decision m2): Literal supplies it in brackets, Balanced says "it is happening", and Readable gives the sense of necessity that the purpose clause carries.

decisions.choice: [esto es] (L); esto sucede (B); tiene que cumplirse (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: se ha vuelto contra mí
decisions.reason: As in English: the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: ameinua kisigino chake dhidi yangu (L, B); amegeuka kunipinga (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of the raised heel, as the English does, since the meaning note explains it; Readable gives its sense, turning against someone. "Amenipiga teke" (has kicked me) would make it an act rather than a hostile turning.

decisions.choice: 빵 for artos (bread)
decisions.reason: 빵 is the current word, as in "생명의 빵" in chapter 6; 떡 is the older Bible word and now means rice cake.

source.text: ἀπ’ ἄρτι λέγω ὑμῖν πρὸ τοῦ γενέσθαι, ἵνα πιστεύσητε ὅταν γένηται ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι.

records.literal_gloss: From now I tell you before the happening, so that you may believe when it happens that I am.

en.L: From now on I am telling you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
en.B: From now on I am telling you before it happens, so that when it does happen you will believe that I am.
en.R: From now on I am telling you things before they happen. Then, when they happen, you will believe that I am.

es.L: Desde ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} lo digo antes de que suceda, para que, cuando suceda, {{plural_you:crean|creáis}} que yo soy.
es.B: Desde ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} lo digo antes de que suceda, para que, cuando suceda, {{plural_you:crean|creáis}} que yo soy.
es.R: Desde ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} digo las cosas antes de que sucedan. Así, cuando sucedan, {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}} que yo soy.

sw.L: Tangu sasa nawaambia kabla halijatokea, ili litakapotokea mpate kuamini kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko.
sw.B: Tangu sasa nawaambia kabla halijatokea, ili litakapotokea kweli mwamini kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko.
sw.R: Tangu sasa nawaambia mambo kabla hayajatokea. Kisha yatakapotokea, mtaamini kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko.

vi.L: Từ nay, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con trước khi việc xảy ra, để khi việc xảy ra, các con tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là [Đấng Hằng Hữu].
vi.B: Từ nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói trước với các con khi việc chưa xảy ra, để khi việc xảy ra, các con sẽ tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đấng Hằng Hữu.
vi.R: Từ nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói trước cho các con biết những việc sắp xảy ra. Rồi khi những việc ấy xảy ra, các con sẽ tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chính là Đấng Hằng Hữu.

ko.L: 지금부터 그 일이 일어나기 전에 내가 너희에게 말한다. 그 일이 일어날 때에 내가 나임을 너희가 믿게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 이제부터 나는 일이 일어나기 전에 너희에게 말해 둔다. 그 일이 일어날 때, 너희가 내가 나임을 믿게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 이제부터 나는 일이 일어나기 전에 너희에게 미리 말해 준다. 그래야 그 일들이 일어날 때, 너희가 내가 나임을 믿게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: from now on: from this point Jesus tells them in advance what is coming
alternatives: now, at this moment, without the sense of continuing
decisions.reason: The phrase most often means "from now on" (14:7; Matthew 26:29, 64). It fits here: starting with the betrayal, Jesus now foretells what will happen, the betrayal (13:21), Peter's denial (13:38) and his own going away (14:29; 16:4), and 14:29 repeats the purpose: "I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe". The phrase can also mean simply "now"; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: that I am: the words God uses of himself, said by Jesus of himself, as in 8:24 and 8:28
alternatives: a plain "that I am he": that I am the one I claim to be, the one Scripture speaks of
decisions.reason: As in 8:24 and 8:28, "I am" stands with nothing after it, and nothing in the sentence supplies a predicate; the nearest is "the one" of the psalm in 13:18, which is the betrayer, not Jesus. See meaning decision m1 at 8:24. The context here strengthens the echo of God's name (meaning decision m3). Some take it plainly as "I am he", the one I say I am; that reading is given in the footnote. Marked uncertain as at 8:24.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 43:10, and Isaiah's theme of the God who announces events before they happen
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 43:10 God says his servants are his witnesses "so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he" (in Greek, "that I am"). The surrounding chapters prove the LORD's claim to be God by his telling of things before they happen (Isaiah 41:22-26; 43:9; 46:9-10; 48:3-5). Jesus does the same: he foretells his betrayal so that, when it comes, his disciples will believe. The betrayal, which might shake their trust, becomes evidence for it.

decisions.choice: that I am, with no "he" supplied
alternatives: that I am who I claim to be
decisions.reason: As at 8:24 and 8:28 (rendering decision r-en-1 at 8:24), every level keeps the bare words, because the echo of God's name is uppermost (meaning decision m2). The footnote gives "that I am he".

decisions.choice: things before they happen ... when they happen
decisions.reason: Readable makes "it" plural to say that from now on he foretells more than one event (meaning decision m1); the betrayal comes first.

decisions.choice: yo soy, with nothing supplied
decisions.reason: The bare "yo soy" used for this saying throughout John (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: mimi niko
decisions.reason: As at 8:24, 28 and 58: the words with which God names himself, with no "he" supplied, as in the English. "Mimi niko" carries the echo of Exodus 3:14 and of Isaiah 43:10, which the meaning notes point to.

decisions.choice: "Ta là [Đấng Hằng Hữu]" (L); "Ta là Đấng Hằng Hữu" (B); "Ta chính là Đấng Hằng Hữu" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "là" cannot stand without a complement, so a bare "Ta là" is not a sentence. "Hằng Hữu" ("the ever-existing one") is the Vietnamese Bible's wording for God's name in Exodus 3:14 and keeps the echo the meaning decision describes; "Ta là Đấng ấy" would give only the plain sense. The same form is used in 8:24 and 8:28; 8:58 says "Ta Hằng Hữu"; 18:5-8, where the plain sense is uppermost, says "Ta đây".

decisions.choice: 내가 나임을 ("that I am"), with no "he" supplied
decisions.reason: As in 8:24 and 8:28 in Korean: the absolute "I am" is kept without a predicate so the echo of God's name stays open, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ λαμβάνων ἄν τινα πέμψω ἐμὲ λαμβάνει, ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ λαμβάνων λαμβάνει τὸν πέμψαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, the [one] receiving whomever I send me receives, the [one] and me receiving receives the [one] having sent me."

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who receives whomever I send receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who welcomes someone I send welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and anyone who welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} welcomes the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: I tell you the truth: when people welcome anyone I send, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are welcoming the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: el que recibe al que yo envíe, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me recibe; y el que a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me recibe, recibe al que me envió».
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el que acoge a alguien que yo envío, me acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; y el que me acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, acoge al que me envió».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: cuando alguien recibe bien a quien yo envío, me está recibiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y cuando alguien me recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, está recibiendo al que me envió».

sw.L: Kweli kweli nawaambia, anayempokea yeyote nitakayemtuma ananipokea {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na anayenipokea {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anampokea yule aliyenituma."
sw.B: Kweli kweli nawaambia, yeyote anayemkaribisha mtu ninayemtuma ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na yeyote anayenikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anamkaribisha yule aliyenituma."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: watu wanapomkaribisha mtu yeyote ninayemtuma, wananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na wanaponikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, wanamkaribisha yule aliyenituma."

vi.L: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai tiếp nhận người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến là tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ai tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là tiếp nhận Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con: Ai tiếp đón người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến là tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ai tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là tiếp đón Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: Khi người ta tiếp đón người nào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến, là họ đang tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và khi họ tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là họ đang tiếp đón Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 내가 보내는 사람을 누구든지 받아들이는 사람은 나를 받아들이는 것이고, 나를 받아들이는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 받아들이는 것이다."
ko.B: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 내가 보내는 사람을 맞아들이는 사람은 나를 맞아들이는 것이고, 나를 맞아들이는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 맞아들이는 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 사람들이 내가 보내는 누군가를 맞아들이면, 그것은 나를 맞아들이는 것이다. 그리고 나를 맞아들이면, 나를 보내신 분을 맞아들이는 것이다."

decisions.choice: the envoy stands for the one who sends him: to receive the envoy is to receive the sender
decisions.reason: In Jewish practice, as across the ancient world, an envoy represented the one who sent him, so that the way he was treated was the way his sender was treated (12:44-45; Matthew 10:40; Luke 10:16). Jesus is the Father's envoy, and his disciples will be his (17:18; 20:21).

decisions.choice: receive: welcome and accept, both as a guest and as one whose message is believed
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:12 ("as many as received him") and 5:43 ("you do not receive me"). It includes taking someone in as a guest, as travelling messengers depended on hospitality, and accepting the one who sent them.

decisions.choice: the saying takes up 13:16: the one sent is not above his sender, yet carries his authority
alternatives: a separate saying with no link to its context
decisions.reason: After the warning about the betrayer (13:18-19), Jesus returns to the picture of 13:16. His disciples are not greater than he is, but those he sends come with his authority and the Father's. The betrayal of one of them does not cancel the mission of the rest.

decisions.choice: welcomes (B), welcome (R); anyone ... someone (B), people ... anyone (R)
decisions.reason: "Welcome" says in everyday English what receiving a messenger meant (meaning decision m2). "Anyone", "someone" and "people" keep the saying general without he or she, so no gender setting is needed. The "Truly, truly" here follows rendering decision r-en-1 at 13:16.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: acoge (B); recibe bien (R); recibe (L)
decisions.reason: Welcome as a guest and as one whose message is believed (meaning decision m2).
